findings.title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header
findings.description: Without HSTS, browsers will happily fall back to plain HTTP for this site, which lets an on-path attacker downgrade the connection and intercept or tamper with traffic (SSL-stripping).
findings.remediation: Add a response header such as 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' once you're confident every subdomain is served over HTTPS.

findings.title: Plain HTTP is served without redirecting to HTTPS
findings.description: The site responds on plain HTTP without redirecting to HTTPS, so a user who types the bare domain (or follows an http:// link) will have their traffic sent unencrypted, exposing it to interception and tampering.
findings.evidence: GET http://example.com did not redirect to https:// (final URL: http://example.com/)
findings.remediation: Configure the web server/load balancer to redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS (301/308), and add HSTS once that's in place.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: Without a CSP, the browser has no server-defined restriction on which scripts/styles/frames can load, which widens the impact of any XSS vulnerability elsewhere on the site.
findings.remediation: Define a Content-Security-Policy appropriate to the site, starting restrictive (e.g. default-src 'self') and loosening only as needed.

findings.title: Missing clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive is set, so the page can be embedded in an iframe on another site and used for a clickjacking attack.
findings.evidence: No X-Frame-Options header and no CSP frame-ancestors directive
findings.remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN if framing by your own site is needed), or set 'frame-ancestors' in your CSP.

findings.title: Server accepts outdated TLS 1.0 connections
findings.description: TLS 1.0 is deprecated and has known weaknesses. Its continued support allows a downgrade attack to force a weaker connection.
findings.evidence: TLS handshake pinned to TLS 1.0 succeeded
findings.remediation: Disable TLS 1.0 in the server's TLS configuration; support only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

findings.title: Server accepts outdated TLS 1.1 connections
findings.description: TLS 1.1 is deprecated and has known weaknesses. Its continued support allows a downgrade attack to force a weaker connection.
findings.evidence: TLS handshake pinned to TLS 1.1 succeeded
findings.remediation: Disable TLS 1.1 in the server's TLS configuration; support only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

findings.title: Server header discloses server/technology details
findings.description: Revealing the exact server software/version (or backend framework) makes it easier for an attacker to look up known vulnerabilities for that specific version.
findings.remediation: Suppress or generalize the Server header at the web server/proxy/framework level.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy header
findings.description: Without a Referrer-Policy, the browser's default behavior may leak the full URL (including sensitive query parameters) to third parties in outbound links and resource requests.
findings.remediation: Add a header such as 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin'.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options header
findings.description: Without 'nosniff', some browsers will try to guess (MIME-sniff) a response's content type, which can turn an upload/reflection endpoint into an XSS vector.

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy header
findings.description: Permissions-Policy lets you explicitly disable powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, etc.) that the site doesn't use, reducing the blast radius of any injected script.
findings.remediation: Add a Permissions-Policy header disabling features the site doesn't need, e.g. 'Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()'.

findings.title: Port 443 (HTTPS) is open
findings.description: HTTPS on port 443 is reachable. Confirm this is intentional and necessary for this host to expose publicly.
findings.remediation: Close this port if it isn't intentionally public, or restrict it with a firewall.
